title: The Day of the Two Puzzle Pieces
skyStory: The moon crawls sideways into Cancer, ninety-five percent full and carrying its home on its back like a hermit crab with a very big shell. Cancer is the sign of home, memory and things kept in drawers for decades. Tonight, Cancer has been rummaging. Something small and lost is about to turn up in two places at once. The candle gasps.

reading: Today you will find a single jigsaw puzzle piece somewhere it has no right to be: a coat pocket, a toolbox, the bottom of a drawer you rarely open. It will be mostly blue, a piece of sky. You will have no idea which puzzle it came from. Keep it.

At some point Nancy will message you about finding a puzzle piece too. Blue. Sky. Possibly a corner. Don't even scream. Okay, a small scream is acceptable. [[The World]] clicks into place in the strangest ways. Set your piece next to the onyx tonight. Cancer says missing pieces always find their people.
joel.mission: Find something lost in the house today, any small thing, and return it to where it belongs, ceremonially.
joel.omen: A blue piece of anything in an odd place. It means a missing piece of a plan is about to appear.

reading: A Cancer moon puts you in a nostalgic mood, and the Wood Rat goes digging. Somewhere in an old bag or a bottom drawer you will find a single puzzle piece, mostly blue, part of a sky. You have no idea where it came from. Hold onto it.

Then the message arrives: Joel found one too. Blue, a piece of sky, at almost the same hour. DES. Your hands will need a minute to recover from all the gesturing. [[The Star]] is shining over two pieces from two different puzzles that are somehow the same sky. Photograph yours and send it over.
nancy.mission: Photograph your puzzle piece, or any small blue thing, next to your ruby and send it to Joel.
nancy.omen: A hermit crab, or a picture of one. It means home is wherever your people are.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's stone for a shared mystery
nancy.elementWhy: home is where the heart lands

together.text: Tonight, each of you tells the other the story of one object you have kept for years for no practical reason. A ticket stub, a button, a shell. Cancer wants the full origin story. Bonus points if your hands knock something over during the telling.
